Replies.Text:
Which editions run the API and MCP, and whether the UI depends on them (asked in the session, 2026-10-29):

The UI is driven by the REST API alone. The page in public/ has no other data path: every list, plan, thread, run and setting is a fetch to /api, and the live updates come over the /api/events stream. In the three apps on the shared page server (Desktop, Sidecar, Client) those calls go through the forwarder at /servers/<key>/api on the app's own loopback origin, which relays them to the server the root names. The Electron bridge carries only app-level things: theme and scale, the remembered view state, the folder picker, Print to PDF, the license token and the close question.

MCP is POST /api/mcp, attached inside Api.Attach, so it is on wherever the API is, with no switch to leave it out. The page never calls it; it is for agents and bin/mcp.js.

Who starts a server:
- Sidecar: always, over the folder, on 127.0.0.1 in the 52000 range. API and MCP on; the page uses that API through the forwarder.
- Desktop: only while a folder is open: the sidecar over that folder in the 3600 range, with the address file. API and MCP on. Connected to a Server, or on a routed folder, it starts nothing and the page uses the Server's API. On the chooser it serves no API.
- Client: never. No API or MCP of its own; the page talks to the added Servers' APIs through the forwarder, the Clerk token on each call.
- Server: always, and it refuses Scope None. Its window loads the page from the server's own address with no forwarder. API and MCP on, behind the gate and the sign-in.

Recommendation for the table: one row, "Web API and MCP", reading Sidecar Yes, Client No, Desktop Yes while a folder is open, Server Yes; the two cannot be separated today, so a row that says MCP No for the Server would need a switch in Api.Attach first. Resolve with no reply to take it.

would it simplify things if we always ran the API/MCP service for each edition. This would allow each edition to support sidecar functionality. we could have the UI always connect to localhost and, in Client and Desktop, can proxy the upstream connection.

Yes, it would simplify things, and most of it is already there. Where things stand: in the Desktop, Sidecar and Client the page already talks to localhost: the page server on 127.0.0.1 (electron/Page.js) forwards /servers/<key>/api and /servers/<key>/instructions to the upstream, headers and streams included. What is missing for an agent beside a Client or a Desktop is three things on that local address: a plain /api (not under /servers/<key>), an /instructions page naming the window's project, and /api/mcp.

What it does not need: a full src/Server.js with a Store in the Client and the Desktop. A proxy edition is the forwarder plus one small adapter: Operations already gives every operation its Method and Path (Operations.Route), so a local MCP endpoint can turn each tools/call into the upstream REST call with the person's session token, and the local /api is the forwarder pointed at the window's one upstream. The identity question has one answer: the local address acts for the signed-in person (the token the window holds goes on every forwarded call), which is the sidecar model, "<service> by <person>". With several projects open (the Desktop), the instructions name the current one and the MCP shim takes --project as it does against a Server.

What it buys: one shape in every edition (localhost API, MCP and instructions), one guide, and the table's Web API and Web MCP cells all Yes. What it costs: the local-only forwarder gaining /api, /instructions and /api/mcp (about one module, electron/Proxy.js), and the Desktop needing a notion of the current project for the instructions.

Recommendation: yes: every edition serves API, MCP and instructions on its localhost address; the Sidecar and the Server as they do now, the Client and the Desktop through the forwarder with the MCP translator, no local Store. It becomes part of the editions cut Step. Resolve with no reply to take it.
